facts.text: Salem is home to the John Hay Center, whose centerpiece is the Stevens Memorial Museum built in 1970 to preserve local history.
The John Hay Center also houses the Genealogical Library, known nationwide for its extensive research materials on Washington County history.
The Depot Railroad Museum in Salem showcases the Monon Railroad era, featuring modern exhibits that bring 19th‑century rail travel to life.
Salem’s downtown district is listed on the National Register of Historic Places, including the historic Washington County Courthouse at the town square.
The birthplace of former U.S. Secretary of State John Hay is a National Historic Site in Salem, preserved since 1971.
Agriculture remains a pillar of Salem’s economy, while diverse industries now provide steady employment for residents.
